reason: E2 directly supports the premise that edge dislocations are prevalent and dominant in a BCC HEA, which is a key part of the hypothesis. However, E1 only reports high strength of an alloy without addressing lattice distortion or dislocation mechanisms, and no cited evidence supports the causal link between lattice distortion and edge dislocation pinning or the predicted effect of compositional modification on strength.
premises: Local lattice distortions from multi-principal element mixing create a heterogeneous atomic landscape that impedes dislocation motion.
Edge dislocations are preferentially impeded and are critical in HEAs, in contrast to typical BCC metals where screw dislocations dominate.
Increasing lattice distortion (e.g., via compositional modification) will increase hardness and yield strength.
The mechanism is intrinsic to single-phase, chemically disordered HEAs and operates under dislocation-mediated plasticity.
